t: 3241. Time Taken to Mark All Nodes
o: Marking spreads outward from the start node: an odd neighbor gets marked 1 step after a marked neighbor, an even neighbor 2 steps. times[i] is the maximum weighted distance from i, where traversing an edge into node v costs 2 if v is even else 1. Brute force DFS from every node is O(n²) — too slow for n = 10⁵ — so we reroot: compute downward depths once, then push parent-side information down, keeping the top two child contributions to exclude self.
k: times[i] = max weighted distance from i with edge weight w(u,v) = 2 if v even else 1.
down[v]: max depth within v's subtree; up[v]: max depth via v's parent.
Rerooting needs top-two down-values per node to exclude the child being updated.

a.i: First compute down[] with a post-order pass over an iterative DFS order. Then in pre-order, for each child c of u, up[c] = max(up[u], best down-contribution among u's children excluding c) + w(u,c). The answer per node is max(down, up). Tracking the two largest child contributions makes each exclusion O(1).
s: Root at 0; get DFS order and parents iteratively.
Post-order: down[u] = max(down[c] + w(u,c)) over children.
Pre-order: for each u compute top two child values d1,d2; for each child c set up[c] = max(up[u], (d1==its value ? d2 : d1)) + w(u,c).
Output max(down[i], up[i]) for all i.
a.t: O(n) — three linear passes over the tree
a.sp: O(n) for adjacency, order, and DP arrays

w: Rerooting is the expected technique; verify with example 3 ([2,4],[0,1],[2,3],[0,2] → [4,6,3,5,5]). Pitfalls: recursion depth on a path-shaped tree (use iterative DFS), and the top-two exclusion when several children tie for the maximum. Follow-up: node weights instead of parity weights, or answering queries on subtrees.
